ci_method: Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021) doubly-robust group-time ATT(g,t) with never-treated counties as the comparison group, aggregated with weights proportional to the number of treated county-years per cohort (the 'simple' aggregation, which exactly reproduces the requested treated-county-year-weighted ATT; verified by hand, weights sum to all 3,185 treated county-years). 95% CI = point estimate +/- 1.96 * SE, where the SE (0.210) comes from the multiplier bootstrap clustered at the county level, 2,000 replications, seed 20261027.
specifications_run: Static TWFE: new_biz_per_10k ~ program | county + year FE, IID SEs -> -0.447 (SE 0.111). DISCARDED: negative weighting / forbidden comparisons (already-treated counties used as controls while effects grow over time) make this wrong-signed.
Static TWFE, same spec with SEs clustered by county -> -0.447 (SE 0.214), 95% CI [-0.868, -0.027]. DISCARDED for the same reason.

TWFE event study, event time binned at [-8, +10], reference period -1, county + year FE -> pre-period coefficients non-zero and erratic (e.g. +1.04 at -5, +0.68 at -4), a known artifact of contaminated comparisons. DISCARDED.
Sun & Abraham (2021) interaction-weighted estimator (fixest sunab), cohort x relative-time interactions, aggregated to overall ATT -> 7.179 (SE 0.162).
Callaway & Sant'Anna, est_method='dr', control_group='nevertreated', 'simple' aggregation -> 7.179 (SE 0.210), CI [6.768, 7.591]. PREFERRED SPECIFICATION.

Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, never-treated, 'dynamic' (event-study) aggregation -> overall 8.199 (SE 0.198). Not used as the headline because it weights each event time equally, which over-weights long exposures rather than treated county-years.

Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, never-treated, 'group' (cohort) aggregation -> reported; cohort ATTs 9.30 (2006), 5.40 (2011), 3.03 (2016), consistent with monotonically growing effects and differing exposure lengths.
Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, control_group='notyettreated', 'simple' aggregation -> 7.038 (SE 0.146).
Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, never-treated, analytic (non-bootstrap) influence-function SEs -> 7.179 (SE 0.209), CI [6.770, 7.589].
Callaway & Sant'Anna, est_method='reg' (outcome regression), never-treated, simple -> 7.179 (SE 0.210).
Callaway & Sant'Anna, est_method='ipw', never-treated, simple -> 7.179 (SE 0.205). (All three estimators coincide because there are no covariates in the data.)
Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, never-treated, base_period='universal' -> 7.179 (SE 0.218).
Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, never-treated, anticipation=1 -> 4.960 (SE 0.213). Mechanically drops the 2006 cohort (it has no pre-period left), so this is a different estimand, not a bias check.

Callaway & Sant'Anna, dr, never-treated, 2006 cohort dropped entirely -> 4.721 (SE 0.192). Reweighting, not bias: recomputing the treated-county-year-weighted average of the FULL model's ATT(g,t) over only the 2011+2016 cohorts gives exactly 4.721.

Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess imputation estimator, implemented manually (county + year FE fit on untreated county-years with FE singletons retained, then averaging y - yhat over all treated county-years) -> 7.025, county-cluster bootstrap (1,000 reps) SE 0.129, percentile CI [6.782, 7.281].

Stacked (cohort-by-cohort) DiD with never-treated controls only, cohort-specific county and year FE, clustered by county -> 4.973, CI [4.786, 5.159]. Different weighting (it equalizes cohorts and truncates exposure windows), reported for completeness.
Placebo 1: 2016-cohort counties + never-treated, years restricted to <=2015, pseudo-adoption year set to 2011 -> -0.041 (SE 0.256), CI [-0.544, 0.461].
Placebo 2: 2011-cohort counties + never-treated, years <=2010, pseudo-adoption 2008 -> -0.044 (SE 0.275), CI [-0.583, 0.496].
Placebo 3: 2011-cohort counties + never-treated, years <=2010, pseudo-adoption 2007 -> 0.208 (SE 0.271), CI [-0.323, 0.740].

Linear differential-trend sensitivity: computed the mean exposure length over treated county-years (7.00 years) and solved for the differential trend that would nullify the estimate (1.026 units/year) or push the CI lower bound to zero (0.967 units/year), then compared it to the pre-trend slope actually estimated from cohorts with testable pre-periods (-0.015 units/year, county-cluster bootstrap CI [-0.052, 0.023]).
assumptions_checked: Data integrity / treatment coding: 4,800 rows = 300 counties x 16 years, perfectly balanced panel, no missing outcomes; the only missing values are adoption_year for the 26 never-treated counties. Reconstructed program from (year >= adoption_year) and got 0 mismatches in 4,800 rows. Treatment is absorbing (no county exits). 3,185 treated county-years.

Rollout structure: only three adoption cohorts - 2006 (146 counties), 2011 (71), 2016 (57) - plus 26 never-treated. Cohort 2006 contributes 2,190 of 3,185 treated county-years (69% of the estimand's weight) and has exactly ONE pre-treatment year (2005), so parallel trends is UNTESTABLE for the majority of the weight. This is the single biggest limitation.

No-anticipation: event-study ATT(g,t) at event time -1 is 0.154 (SE 0.240) for never-treated controls and 0.029 (SE 0.231) for not-yet-treated; at -2 it is -0.150 (SE 0.262). No pre-period jump. Also re-estimated allowing one anticipation period (spec above).

Parallel trends, formal test: Callaway-Sant'Anna Wald pre-test across all 15 estimable pre-treatment ATT(g,t) gives p = 0.692. Max absolute pre-period ATT(g,t) is 0.452, mean 0.063, SD 0.279 - all individually indistinguishable from zero, with no drift pattern.

Parallel trends, visual/event-study: dynamic aggregation gives pre-period coefficients from event time -10 to -1 all within [-0.45, +0.42] and flat, then a clean monotone ramp post-treatment (+1.04 at 0, +5.20 at +4, +11.26 at +10, +15.61 at +14). Same picture with not-yet-treated controls.

Parallel trends, placebo re-assignment: three placebo designs that shift adoption 3-5 years earlier within pre-treatment windows all return effects near zero (-0.04, -0.04, +0.21) with CIs containing zero and excluding anything close to the estimated 7.18.

Parallel trends, magnitude sensitivity: a differential linear trend of about 1.03 units/year between treated and never-treated counties would be required to explain away the entire estimate. That is roughly 20x larger than the upper end of the pre-trend slope actually measured (CI [-0.052, 0.023]). The result is not fragile to plausible trend violations in the testable cohorts.

Heterogeneous / dynamic treatment effects (the TWFE failure mode): effects grow roughly linearly in exposure, about +1.05 units per additional year, with no plateau through 15 years. Confirmed this is what drives static TWFE to -0.45: the 2006 cohort serves as a 'control' with a rising outcome for the later cohorts, generating large negative weights. This is why no TWFE specification is used for the headline number.

Estimator robustness: Callaway-Sant'Anna (dr/reg/ipw, never-treated and not-yet-treated, universal base period), Sun-Abraham, and BJS imputation all land in 7.02-7.18. The estimand is robust to the choice of modern heterogeneity-robust estimator.

Inference robustness: compared multiplier-bootstrap SEs clustered at county (0.210), analytic influence-function SEs (0.209), and a nonparametric county-cluster bootstrap for the imputation estimator (0.129). Serial correlation within county is accounted for by clustering at county; conclusions are unchanged.

Comparison-group adequacy: the never-treated group is only 26 counties (8.7% of the sample), and long-run ATT(g,t) for the 2006 cohort requires extrapolating that small group's trajectory 15 years forward. Cross-checked against not-yet-treated controls (7.038), which widens the early-period comparison pool and gives a very similar answer.

Noise level / external plausibility: residual SD around the event-study fit is 0.96 against an outcome SD of 6.09, so the signal-to-noise ratio is unusually high and the CI is correspondingly tight for 300 counties. The implied effect (+7.2 on a pre-treatment base of about 11, i.e. roughly +65%, rising to more than a doubling by year 15) is very large for a small-business grant program; the statistical evidence is strong but the magnitude is worth sanity-checking against program scale and the registration-data definition before publication.
headline_claim: Across all county-years in which a county was enrolled, the small-business grant program raised new business registrations by an average of 7.2 per 10,000 residents (95% CI 6.8 to 7.6), with effects that start small in the adoption year and grow by roughly one registration per 10,000 residents for each additional year of participation.
